questions.q: What does this recap say Chapter 1 actually was, structurally?
options: A single lesson repeated 24 times with minor variations
A chapter with no relationship to the four case studies
24 unrelated topics with no connection between them
One connected argument where each lesson supplied a piece the next one needed, not 24 separate unrelated topics
questions.explain: Requirements and estimation fed storage and processing choices, which fed Lambda/Kappa, partitioning, layers, and the trade-off lessons in turn.

questions.q: What does it mean that all four case studies drew from the "same toolbox" but landed on different designs?
options: Different requirements produced different correct designs, even though every case study used the same set of underlying concepts
The four case studies actually used completely unrelated sets of concepts
All four case studies ended up with an identical architecture
Only one of the four case studies used any concepts from earlier lessons
questions.explain: Ride-sharing fit Kappa, fraud detection was streaming-only and AP, retail inventory justified Lambda, and social media's problem was pure volume.

questions.q: According to this recap, what is the actual transferable skill from this chapter?
options: Knowing the lesson numbers of this chapter by heart
The four-step process from Lesson 24, applied with this chapter's vocabulary as the material that fills it in for a new scenario
Reciting the definitions from the Key Terms tables word for word
Memorizing the exact architecture used in each of the four case studies
questions.explain: The goal was never a memorized fixed answer — it's running the same process against something never seen before.

questions.q: What comes immediately after Chapter 1 in this course, per this recap?
options: The course ends here with no further chapters
Chapter 2: DP-700 Certification Prep
A return to Lesson 1 for review before continuing
A second, entirely separate System Design chapter
questions.explain: Chapter 1 (System Design for Data Engineers) is explicitly complete, and Chapter 2 turns this knowledge toward DP-700 exam prep.

questions.q: Which case study did this recap identify as leaning AP on purpose, and why?
options: Fraud detection, because refusing to score during a partition would block legitimate transactions for no real benefit
Ride-sharing, because it had no relationship to the CAP theorem
None of the four case studies involved a CAP trade-off
Retail inventory, because it required perfectly consistent data at all times
questions.explain: Fraud detection (Lesson 21) and social media (Lesson 23) both leaned AP; fraud detection did so specifically to avoid blocking legitimate purchases.
